chapter: New Orleans scene and jazz club
title: Pianist Burnell Santiago
summary: A young prodigy pianist, his style, early death, and attempts to reach his widow.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I don't think he was, but he used to sit in the arrogant and all. When you talk about piano players, there's a piano player that I'd like you to hear sometimes. He's a colored fellow. His name is Noel Fusher. He was raised with Lloyd Primm and all of us. Yeah, I don't know him. No, I don't think he did. He had a civil service job. He used to work under me over the port. His uncle played up and he used to call him all this. He used to call Bill Willie. He'd talk about fine kind of thing. It was Bornell Santiago, your man, Borough.
I knew his brother, but I never met him in time. Blackie, I knew him.

Yeah, but this boy was a handsome boy. He could pass the Spanish. He played with us a lot, but then he started to pull up that dope and that was it. He died young, but I don't remember him when he was four years old and playing piano. He couldn't even reach the pedals. He was a little bit of a piano player. They tried to make something out of him. Armstrong came in and heard him. A few of those big bands heard him and all. I don't want to learn how to read. But boy, he had a style. He'd make that piano rock. He was only about 112 pounds. Boy, I was talking about a man of a Harlem house. A hard society. Variations and all. And is he a wasn't even getting Pushy. He has a style or something like that. Yeah, but I'd like to hear him. In fact, he stayed at the house of Faisal who stayed in the noise line street. I think it was 19...07, I think. Or 1915.
Well I must know somebody from that neighborhood.
Well I mean, you can contact me and I can contact you for you.

Well you know, I heard a home-made record of Burnell about 9 days ago up in Little Rock, a guy named John Reed. See, he was a friend of Willie Santiago, who was an uncle. Yeah, Willie. So I called up Chinese Santiago, who was the sister. She's married to a trumpet player named Picki. Anyway, she said that Burnell's widow had a... She could get in touch with his widow because I found out when I was in office, that his widow had a lot of them. It must have been great.

Oh he was, he was tough. It was a shame that he had to go that fast. He used to stay up across the street in the house then. Boy they had all kinds of bands and every week. They had either a party or a fish fry or something else. And then there was another piano player, we used to call it Plutzum. He had a hunk, he was back on the hill. He played a fine piano. But this little Willie, I didn't see, I didn't know what this is. That's Push's uncle up, he played a very fine piano.
